title: The duty to fight and the yoga of understanding

verses.sa: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
verses.tr: All beings are unmanifest before birth and unmanifest after death; they are manifest only in between. Why grieve over that?
verses.angle: Avyaktam: the unmanifest state before birth and after death
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that death is certain for the born and birth for the dead. Now he speaks of the hidden state that frames all life.

body.text: All beings are unmanifest before birth and unmanifest after death; they are manifest only in between. Why grieve over that? Krishna uses the word avyaktam, the unmanifest. He says that before birth and after death, beings are simply unmanifest, and only briefly visible in between. He now turns to the inner self that is seen as wondrous by those who seek it.

verses.sa: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः । आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोतिश्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥
verses.tr: Some behold the inner being as wondrous; some speak of it as wondrous; some hear of it as wondrous; and even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
verses.angle: Even after hearing, no one truly knows
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his teaching on the self, showing that it is beyond ordinary thought.

body.text: Some behold the inner being as wondrous; some speak of it as wondrous; some hear of it as wondrous; and even after hearing, no one truly knows it. Even after hearing about the self, no one truly knows it. The self is wondrous to behold, describe, and hear about, yet it remains difficult to fully grasp. Krishna then tells Arjuna that the self in every body is eternal and cannot be slain. Listen to his next words.

verses.sa: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.tr: O descendant of Bharata, the embodied one in every body is eternal and cannot be slain. Therefore you should not grieve for any being.
verses.angle: Dehi: the embodied one cannot be slain
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna is drowning in sorrow, but Krishna answers with one truth. Listen for the word that ends the argument about grief.

body.text: O descendant of Bharata, the embodied one in every body is eternal and cannot be slain. Therefore you should not grieve for any being. Krishna closes with one word, dehi, the embodied one. The body may fall, but the one who lives inside every body is eternal, so there is no reason to weep. Krishna now turns from grief to duty, and tells Arjuna to consider his own role as a warrior.

verses.sa: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि । धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
verses.tr: Considering your own duty, you should not waver. For a warrior, no action is more beneficial than a righteous battle.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna is frozen on the battlefield, and Krishna speaks directly to his hesitation. Listen to how Krishna defines the warrior's path.

body.text: Considering your own duty, you should not waver. For a warrior, no action is more beneficial than a righteous battle. Krishna uses the word svadharma, one's own duty. For Arjuna, that duty is not to avoid the fight, but to fight it, because no action serves a warrior better than a righteous battle. Krishna then describes this war not as a burden, but as an open gate to higher realms for the warrior who receives it.

verses.sa: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् । सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
verses.tr: An unbidden battle is an open gate to higher realms. O Partha, fortunate are the warriors who receive such a war.
verses.angle: Yadrichchhaya: the unbidden gate to heaven
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one word that turns the war from a burden into a gift. Listen closely for what he calls this unbidden battle.

body.text: An unbidden battle is an open gate to higher realms. O Partha, fortunate are the warriors who receive such a war. The word to notice is yadrichchhaya, meaning unbidden. It means this war came to them without asking, yet Krishna calls it an open gate to higher realms, framing the conflict as a rare gift of duty. Krishna then warns that refusing this war would mean abandoning duty and honor.

verses.sa: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि । ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.tr: If you do not fight this righteous war, you will abandon your duty and honor and incur blame.
verses.angle: Swadharma and kirti, the two things to lose
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just called this a righteous war. Now he warns Arjuna about the cost of refusing it. Listen to the two things he says will be lost.

body.text: If you do not fight this righteous war, you will abandon your duty and honor and incur blame. Krishna names two things, swadharma and kirti, your own duty and your honor, and says that abandoning both is the sin. The blame is not for fighting, but for running away from the role you were born to carry. He adds that everyone will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.

verses.sa: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् । संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
verses.tr: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his argument by warning Arjuna about the world outside the chariot. Listen for the exact comparison he makes between dying and living with shame.

body.text: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death. Krishna says the disgrace will be aviyam, everlasting. For a man honored as you are, that endless shame is worse than death. He shifts the argument from your inner duty to how the world will judge you. The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear, and those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.

verses.sa: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः । येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
verses.tr: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.
verses.angle: Maharathah: how great warriors read fear
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What happens to a warrior's name when he stops fighting? Listen to how Krishna warns him that the great warriors will think he withdrew from battle out of fear.

body.text: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in high regard will see you as small. The word Maharathah means great chariot-warriors, and laabhavam means smallness or a drop in status. Those who once held him in high regard will see him reduced to nothing. Krishna asks what could be more painful than enemies mocking a warrior's strength.

verses.sa: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः । निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
verses.tr: Your enemies will speak many unworthy words, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?
verses.angle: Your enemies will mock your strength
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks what could hurt more than public shame. Listen to the exact words he uses.

body.text: Your enemies will speak many unworthy words, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that? He names two things: unworthy words and mockers of your strength. The verse says your enemies will speak many such words, and asks what could be more painful. Krishna then shifts to the two possible results of the battle, death or victory.

verses.sa: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् । तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
verses.tr: If you are killed, you will attain heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the kingdom. Therefore, rise, Kaunteya, and fight with resolve.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for one word that turns Arjuna's fear into a command to stand up, no matter what the outcome is.

body.text: If you are killed, you will attain heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the kingdom. Therefore, rise, Kaunteya, and fight with resolve. The word is kritanishchayah, firm resolve. Krishna tells Arjuna to make up his mind and fight, because the decision itself is what matters. Krishna then tells Arjuna to treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same.

verses.sa: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.tr: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then enter the battle; you will not incur wrongdoing.
verses.angle: samam: equal, making all pairs one
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna to treat victory and defeat, gain and loss, as equal before entering the battle.

body.text: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then enter the battle; you will not incur wrongdoing. Listen to the word samam, equal. Krishna places pleasure and pain, gain and loss, and victory and defeat in a single line as equal. This is the exact condition he gives before Arjuna must fight. Krishna now turns to the method of yoga to help Arjuna cast off the bondage of action.

verses.sa: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु । बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
verses.tr: This wisdom has been taught to you in Sankhya. Now hear it in yoga. Equipped with this understanding, Arjuna, you will cast off the bondage of action.
verses.angle: Sankhya to yoga, knowledge to action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns the conversation from knowing to doing. He promises that this same wisdom will free Arjuna from the trap of his own actions.

body.text: This wisdom has been taught to you in Sankhya. Now hear it in yoga. Equipped with this understanding, Arjuna, you will cast off the bondage of action. The word buddhi, wisdom, appears twice in this verse. Krishna is not giving Arjuna new knowledge, but a new way to use the same understanding. He assures Arjuna that even a small effort in this path will protect him from the greatest fear.

verses.sa: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verses.tr: In this human world, no effort toward this steady wisdom is ever lost. No harmful result comes from it. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that even a tiny step on this path is never wasted. Listen for the exact words of that promise.

body.text: In this human world, no effort toward this steady wisdom is ever lost. No harmful result comes from it. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear. The verse opens with a double negative, na abhiskrama-nasho nasti and na pratyavayo na vidyate, meaning there is no loss of beginning effort and no reverse result. It is a complete guarantee that a small start in this dharma never goes to waste and never backfires. Krishna then contrasts this resolute, one-pointed intellect with an endless, many-branched one. Listen for that distinction.
